description: We are a team of developers passionate about software engineering, AI, and space exploration. Our project, CLPS Lunar Landing Site Navigator, uses NASA/JPL data and scientific calculations to analyze lunar landing sites, sunlight availability, Earth visibility, solar power, and communication opportunities. We combine web development, Python, data analysis, and scientific visualization to support better-informed decisions for future lunar missions.
summary:
CLPS Lunar Navigator is a web-based tool designed to help users explore and compare potential lunar landing sites. It uses NASA data and scientific calculations to study sunlight availability, Earth visibility, terrain obstacles, and communication opportunities at different locations on the Moon.

The platform helps users identify suitable landing areas by analyzing solar power conditions and direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows. Users can compare multiple sites, explore interactive lunar maps, view scientific results, and export mission data as CSV files.

By combining real NASA datasets with interactive visualizations and calculations, CLPS Lunar Navigator makes complex lunar mission planning easier to understand. It supports better decision-making for future lunar missions by helping identify locations with suitable lighting and communication conditions.
details:
Project Details — CLPS Lunar Navigator

1. What Does the Project Do?

CLPS Lunar Navigator is an interactive web application designed to support the exploration and comparison of potential lunar landing sites, with a focus on the Moon’s South Pole. Choosing a suitable landing site is a major challenge because a location must provide more than a safe surface. It also needs reliable sunlight for solar power, clear visibility of Earth for communication, and suitable terrain conditions.

Our project brings these important factors together in one platform. Users can select lunar locations, choose a time period, run scientific calculations, and explore the results through interactive maps, charts, and comparison tools.

2. How Does It Work?

The application combines NASA scientific data with astronomical and terrain calculations.

  • Sunlight Analysis: It calculates the apparent position of the Sun relative to each selected lunar location and studies how sunlight changes over time. This helps estimate when solar panels can receive sunlight.
  • Terrain and Horizon Analysis: Using Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data, the application studies the surrounding terrain and identifies high areas that may block sunlight.
  • Earth Visibility: It calculates the apparent position of Earth from each lunar site and evaluates when Earth is visible above the local horizon.
  • Communication Analysis: It estimates potential Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows and considers terrain obstructions and radio link factors.
  • Solar Power Estimation: It uses solar irradiance and the angle of sunlight to estimate the solar energy available to a lander.
  • Site Comparison: Users can compare up to four locations across different mission conditions and time periods.

The platform also allows users to view scientific results, explore visual representations, review assumptions and methodology, and export mission data in CSV format for further analysis.

3. What Benefits Does It Have?

CLPS Lunar Navigator makes complex lunar environmental information easier to explore and understand. Instead of examining sunlight, terrain, and communication conditions separately, users can study them together.

Its main benefits include:

  • Helping users identify locations with better sunlight conditions.
  • Showing when Earth may be visible from a selected landing site.
  • Identifying terrain that could create visibility or communication problems.
  • Supporting comparisons between multiple landing locations.
  • Providing downloadable scientific data for further research.
  • Making lunar mission planning concepts more accessible through an interactive interface.

4. What Is the Intended Impact?

Our goal is to support better-informed decisions for future lunar exploration, especially missions targeting the challenging South Pole region.

The platform can help students, researchers, and space enthusiasts understand why landing-site selection is complex and how environmental conditions affect lunar missions. It also provides a foundation that could be expanded with additional datasets, higher-resolution terrain models, and more advanced mission-planning capabilities.

We aim to turn complex space data into useful information that people can explore, compare, and understand.

5. What Tools and Technologies Did We Use?

We developed the project using a combination of scientific computing and modern web technologies:

  • Python: Backend calculations and scientific data processing.
  • NASA/JPL NAIF SPICE and SpiceyPy: Astronomical position and coordinate calculations.
  • NASA/JPL Horizons: An alternative source for planetary and lunar position data.
  • NumPy: Numerical calculations and data processing.
  • React and TypeScript: Building the interactive user interface.
  • Node.js and Express: Backend services and API communication.
  • Vite and Tailwind CSS: Development tools and interface styling.
  • GeoTIFF.js: Reading and processing lunar elevation data.

We also used NASA datasets and resources, including LOLA elevation models and the LRO WAC South Pole Mosaic.

6. What Makes Our Project Creative and Innovative?

The main creative idea behind CLPS Lunar Navigator is bringing several important lunar landing-site conditions into one interactive decision-support platform.

Rather than presenting users with separate datasets or static maps, we connect astronomical calculations, terrain analysis, sunlight estimation, and Earth visibility in a single workflow.

One important feature is the ability to compare up to four lunar locations under selected time conditions. This allows users to explore how the same location can have different environmental conditions at different times, and how two locations can offer different advantages.

We also focused on making scientific information understandable. Interactive maps, visual results, clear explanations, and CSV exports help users move from simply viewing data to exploring and comparing it.

7. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

During development, we considered several factors that affect lunar landing-site suitability:

  • Time: Sunlight and Earth visibility change throughout the lunar day and over longer periods.
  • Location: Different landing sites have different environmental conditions.
  • Terrain: Mountains and elevated areas may block sunlight or the line of sight to Earth.
  • Solar Energy: A lander may need sufficient sunlight to support its solar power system.
  • Communication: Maintaining a suitable communication path to Earth is important for mission operations.
  • Scientific Accuracy: We used NASA data, documented assumptions, and scientific methods to make our calculations more meaningful.
  • Usability: We designed the application to make complex scientific analysis accessible through a simple and interactive experience.
